{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts lag behind price turning points, especially at market bottoms where true outcomes bottom before and above model predictions.",
    "When sentiment turns positive (score >= 0.67), model under-forecasts prices by 0.3-0.5% relative to true values which lead with slightly higher lows.",
    "Negative sentiment (score <= 0) has no discernible effect on model accuracy - prices follow mean-reversion patterns regardless of sentiment signal.",
    "Model equilibrium levels are consistently 0.3-0.6% below actual prices during declining phases, with the gap widening to 0.8-1.0% at true outcome lows.",
    "When history shows a clear downtrend, model forecasts are approximately 0.4-0.7% too high relative to genuinely supportable levels.",
    "Sentiment score of 1.00 (strong bull) aligns with true outcomes that are 0.2-0.4% higher than model for the first 10-15 days, then diverges as reality catches up.",
    "Mean-reversion bias in model causes it to undershoot true outcomes during price consolidation by approximately 0.3-0.5% on average."
] }
